![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14165105/assets/a56bcec93b5cc66ef8238b7fe7b213c5e184f1cf4b11baf4524525a63a284780.png)

Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A,$ where the region $D$ is enclosed between two circles centered at $O$ of radii $1$ and $3,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We need to change the coordinate system from Cartesian coordinates to polar coordinates. To do this, we will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Notice that the region $D$ represents the annulus between the disks of radii $1$ and $3$ centered at the origin. 

Cartesian and polar coordinates are connected by the following equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's now write our curves in polar coordinates.

- For ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1,$ we obtain $r=1.$

- For ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9,$ we obtain $r=3.$

As a result, the region can be expressed in polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$ as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 3,\,0\le \theta <2\pi \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{3}\sqrt{{r}^{2}}\cdot r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{3}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{[\frac{{r}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(9-\frac{1}{3})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{26}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{26}{3}[\theta ]_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{26}{3}\cdot 2\pi  \\  & =\frac{52\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
